title: Ezekiel 48:8–22
context: The Lord GOD describes the offering set apart between Judah and Benjamin: a holy portion for the priests, the sons of Zadok, with the sanctuary in its middle; a portion for the Levites that may not be sold or exchanged; a common area for the city, its pasture lands, and those who labor there from all the tribes; and the remainder on either side for the prince (cf. 45:1–8), in a square and orderly arrangement centered on the sanctuary.

verses.text: “By the border of Judah, from the east side to the west side, shall be the offering which you shall offer, twenty-five thousand reeds in width, and in length as one of the portions, from the east side to the west side; and the sanctuary shall be in the middle of it.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Judah, from the east side to the west side, shall be the offering which you shall offer,” with “the sanctuary …in the middle of it.” Arminian readers note that the holy portion sits at the center of the land.

The arrangement echoes 45:1.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see God’s dwelling placed at the heart of his people’s life.

Shared ground: both traditions agree that the central place of the sanctuary pictures the LORD’s presence among the tribes.

verses.text: “The offering that you shall offer to the LORD shall be twenty-five thousand reeds in length, and ten thousand in width.
verses.arminianNotes:
“The offering that you shall offer to the LORD shall be twenty-five thousand reeds in length, and ten thousand in width.” Arminian readers note that the land itself is offered to the LORD.

The measurement repeats 45:1.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the people’s land consecrated at its center.

Shared ground: both traditions read the measurements as part of the vision’s order and avoid building doctrine on the exact numbers.

verses.text: For these, even for the priests, shall be the holy offering: toward the north twenty-five thousand in length, and toward the west ten thousand in width, and toward the east ten thousand in width, and toward the south twenty-five thousand in length; and the sanctuary of the LORD shall be in the middle of it.
verses.arminianNotes:
The holy offering is “for the priests,” and “the sanctuary of the LORD shall be in the middle of it.” Arminian readers note the repeated emphasis on the sanctuary at the center.

The four sides are measured.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the priests’ portion surrounding the place of worship.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as highlighting that worship of the LORD is central to the life of the restored people.

verses.text: It shall be for the priests who are sanctified of the sons of Zadok, who have kept my instruction, who didn’t go astray when the children of Israel went astray, as the Levites went astray.
verses.arminianNotes:
The portion is for “the priests who are sanctified of the sons of Zadok, who have kept my instruction.” Arminian readers note the reference back to 44:10–15.

Faithfulness during Israel’s straying is remembered.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the LORD honoring those who remained faithful.

Shared ground: both traditions agree that the verse connects privilege with faithfulness, and both name 44:15 without expanding the distinction between priests and Levites.

verses.text: It shall be to them an offering from the offering of the land, a most holy thing, by the border of the Levites.
verses.arminianNotes:
The priests’ land is “an offering from the offering of the land,” lying “by the border of the Levites.” Arminian readers note the layers of holiness in the arrangement.

The priests’ land lies within the larger offering.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see degrees of holiness around the sanctuary.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as part of the ordered holiness of the vision, held under the different overall readings of chapters 40–48.

verses.text: “Alongside the border of the priests, the Levites shall have twenty-five thousand cubits in length and ten thousand in width. All the length shall be twenty-five thousand, and the width ten thousand.
verses.arminianNotes:
“Alongside the border of the priests, the Levites shall have twenty-five thousand cubits in length and ten thousand in width.” Arminian readers note that the Levites receive land beside the priests.

Their portion matches the priests’ in size.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the Levites provided for in the arrangement.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as describing the Levites’ place near the sanctuary, without pressing the numbers further.

verses.text: They shall sell none of it, nor exchange it, nor shall the first fruits of the land be alienated, for it is holy to the LORD.
verses.arminianNotes:
“They shall sell none of it, nor exchange it, nor shall the first fruits of the land be alienated, for it is holy to the LORD.” Arminian readers note that the land is not theirs to trade.

It belongs to the LORD.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see stewardship rather than ownership of what is holy.

Shared ground: both traditions agree that what is set apart for the LORD is not to be treated as ordinary property.

verses.text: “The five thousand cubits that are left in the width, in front of the twenty-five thousand, shall be for common use, for the city, for dwelling and for pasture lands; and the city shall be in the middle of it.
verses.arminianNotes:
“The five thousand cubits that are left …shall be for common use, for the city, for dwelling and for pasture lands.” Arminian readers note that the city lies outside the holy portion.

Its land is for ordinary use.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise note the distinction between the sanctuary and the city.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as placing the city near but not within the holy portion, a detail held under several readings of the vision.

verses.text: These shall be its measurements: the north side four thousand and five hundred, and the south side four thousand and five hundred, and on the east side four thousand and five hundred, and the west side four thousand and five hundred.
verses.arminianNotes:
“These shall be its measurements: the north side four thousand and five hundred,” and so on for each side. Arminian readers note that the city is a perfect square.

The square suggests order and completeness.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see a symmetrical design.

Shared ground: both traditions note that Revelation 21 also describes a city with equal sides (cf. Rev 21:16), named here without harmonizing the passages.

verses.text: The city shall have pasture lands: toward the north two hundred fifty, and toward the south two hundred fifty, and toward the east two hundred fifty, and toward the west two hundred fifty.
verses.arminianNotes:
“The city shall have pasture lands: toward the north two hundred fifty,” and likewise on every side. Arminian readers note the open land around the city.

The pattern is again symmetrical.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise read the pasture lands as part of an ordered design.

Shared ground: both traditions treat the measurements simply and avoid attaching symbolism to the specific numbers.

verses.text: The remainder of the length, alongside the holy offering, shall be ten thousand eastward and ten thousand westward; and it shall be alongside the holy offering. Its increase shall be for food to those who labor in the city.
verses.arminianNotes:
The land beside the holy offering is for food: “Its increase shall be for food to those who labor in the city.” Arminian readers note the provision for the city’s workers.

Labor and provision are joined.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see God providing for the daily needs of those who serve the city.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as a picture of ordered provision within the community.

verses.text: Those who labor in the city, out of all the tribes of Israel, shall cultivate it.
verses.arminianNotes:
“Those who labor in the city, out of all the tribes of Israel, shall cultivate it.” Arminian readers note that the city’s workers come from every tribe.

The city belongs to the whole people.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the city as shared by all the tribes rather than one.

Shared ground: both traditions agree that the verse pictures unity among the tribes around a common city.

verses.text: All the offering shall be a square of twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand. You shall offer it as a holy offering, with the possession of the city.
verses.arminianNotes:
“All the offering shall be a square of twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand.” Arminian readers note that the whole holy portion with the city forms a square.

The design is complete and balanced.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see order and holiness joined in the vision.

Shared ground: both traditions read the square as an image of completeness, without building further doctrine on the measurements.

verses.text: “The remainder shall be for the prince, on the one side and on the other of the holy offering and of the possession of the city; in front of the twenty-five thousand of the offering toward the east border, and westward in front of the twenty-five thousand toward the west border, alongside the portions, it shall be for the prince. The holy offering and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the middle of it.
verses.arminianNotes:
“The remainder shall be for the prince, on the one side and on the other of the holy offering.” Arminian readers note that the prince’s land frames the holy portion (cf. 45:7–8).

His portion is defined so that he will not take others’ land.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the prince given a fixed share.

Shared ground: both traditions note that the identity of the prince in chapters 40–48 is discussed, and both read his provision as part of a just order (cf. 45:8).

verses.text: Moreover, from the possession of the Levites, and from the possession of the city, being in the middle of that which is the prince’s, between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin, shall be for the prince.
verses.arminianNotes:
The prince’s portion lies “between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin.” Arminian readers note that the holy portion and city are surrounded by the prince’s land.

Judah and Benjamin border the center.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the arrangement placing worship and city at the heart of the land.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as completing the description of the central area before the remaining tribes are listed.
